Chart with its tools and downloads

Source: R/chart-coverage_downloads.R
cd_coverage_plot_ui.Rd

One chart with the tools every Countdown chart has: a panel to customize how it looks, a download of the chart as a picture, and a download of its data as an Excel workbook. The page gives the data and says how to draw it, and this module does the rest. It is the chart that goes in the tabs of cd_tabbed_charts_ui(), and it works as well on its own in a card.

Usage

cd_coverage_plot_ui(id, toolbar_inline = FALSE)

cd_coverage_plot_toolbar_ui(id)

cd_coverage_plot_server(
  id,
  filename,
  data_fn,
  ...,
  sheet_name,
  i18n,
  plot_fun = NULL,
  about = NULL
)

Arguments

id

The module's id.

toolbar_inline

Logical. FALSE (the default) draws the tools over the chart. TRUE leaves them out, for a page that places them with cd_coverage_plot_toolbar_ui().

filename

A reactive that returns the first part of the downloaded files' name. The date and time and the extension are added to it.

data_fn

A reactive that returns the data the chart draws. It is also what the Excel download holds.

...

Arguments for plot(), used only when plot_fun is NULL.

sheet_name

A reactive that returns the name of the sheet in the Excel download. It comes after ..., so it must be given by name, as must i18n, plot_fun and about.

i18n

The app's translator (a shiny.i18n translator), used for every label.

plot_fun

A function function(d) that takes the data and draws the chart or returns a ggplot. NULL (the default) draws plot(d, ...).

about

What the chart is, for the app's AI: NULL (the default), a list, or a function that returns a list. See datasuite.ui::ai_register_component().

Value

cd_coverage_plot_ui() returns the UI as Shiny tags: the chart, with its tools unless toolbar_inline is TRUE.

cd_coverage_plot_toolbar_ui() returns the chart's tools alone, as Shiny tags.

cd_coverage_plot_server() returns nothing useful. It is called for what it does.

Details

The chart is drawn with plot_fun(data_fn()) once data_fn() has a value. When plot_fun is NULL it is drawn with plot(data_fn(), ...), so the data must then have a plot() method.

The Excel download holds data_fn() on one sheet named sheet_name(). The picture is the chart as it is on screen, as a PNG file. Both files are named filename() followed by the date and time.

In an app made with cd_app(), what the reader changes in the customize panel is kept in the dataset. The chart is also registered with the app's AI bridge, which can then list it and read its data.

By default the tools sit over a corner of the chart. With toolbar_inline = TRUE, cd_coverage_plot_ui() leaves them out, and the page puts them somewhere else (a card's header, for example) with cd_coverage_plot_toolbar_ui(), called with the same id.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# in a page's ui
cd_coverage_plot_ui(ns("coverage"))

# in the page's server
cd_coverage_plot_server("coverage",
  filename = reactive("penta3_coverage"),
  data_fn = reactive(my_coverage_data(cache())),
  sheet_name = reactive(i18n$t("opt_penta3")),
  i18n = i18n,
  plot_fun = function(d) plot(d, title = "Penta3 coverage")
)
} # }
